transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I explain this okay... but, well, I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. It's probably nothing too crazy, but I work in meat processing, and... well, I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or my end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I just... I always seem to leave out the last parts. 

It's really embarrassing to admit, because I know my job completely depends on finishing those things correctly. I try so hard to get it right, I really do, I just... I don't know why I keep missing the ends of my tasks. Is that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing I should be talking to you about?
Did you have similar trouble finishing your schoolwork or chores when you were a child?

Um... yeah, I guess I did. I mean, I was a really good kid, I promise! I wasn't trying to be difficult or anything. But... well, my mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade? And, um, they usually said I was bright—which was really nice of them to say!—but that I needed, like, constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn in my homework. 

It's a little embarrassing to think back on. I remember I would understand the lessons perfectly fine, but I'd just... somehow miss chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was standing right next to me to keep me on track. I really wanted to do a good job for them, just like I do at work now, but... yeah, I guess it has been happening for a while. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have trouble sitting still?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty good at sitting quietly. I try really hard not to be a bother to anyone around me, you know? I don't really get up and run around or anything like that. I might, um, maybe twirl my hair a little bit or doodle on my notepad if I'm trying to focus during a long meeting, but I really try to keep it to myself so I don't distract anyone else. 

I'm definitely not one of those people who's always bouncing off the walls or anything. I can sit still for a long time if I need to. Is... is it okay if I don't have that problem? I know some people with focus issues are really hyper, but I'm honestly pretty calm most of the time. I hope that's an okay answer.
